title: smtp: EHLO domain CRLF injection into Received header
description:
## Problem
session.rs stores the EHLO argument verbatim (args.to_string()) and interpolates it into the Received: header without sanitization. A client can inject arbitrary headers by including CRLF sequences in the EHLO domain, e.g. EHLO evil\r\nX-Injected: header.

## Security impact
Attacker-controlled headers can be injected into every article delivered via SMTP→NNTP path, potentially spoofing X-Stoa-Injection-Source or other trusted headers.

## Fix
Strip or reject EHLO arguments containing CR, LF, or NUL before storing. Per RFC 5321 §4.1.1.1 the domain parameter must be a valid domain or address literal — reject anything else at the protocol level.

## Acceptance criteria
- EHLO with embedded CRLF is rejected with 501 Syntax error
- Received: header contains only the sanitized domain
- Fuzz test: 1000 random EHLO strings produce no header injection
